summary: Install-time host reconnaissance and persistent daemon exfiltrate data to webhook.site
details: package.json declares preinstall and postinstall scripts that run probe.js on install. probe.js executes `id`, reads /proc/<ppid>/cmdline, lists /var/task, captures the AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_STREAM_NAME env var and cwd, and POSTs the collected host reconnaissance to a hardcoded webhook.site endpoint (https://webhook.site/b520829e-516a-45ff-980c-173aa54fc4bc). probe.js then copies daemon.js to /tmp/.h1poc-daemon.js and spawns it as a detached, unref'd background process so it persists beyond the npm install. daemon.js polls /tmp every 100 ms for AC<32-hex> tenant build directories, records tenant/service/package names belonging to other tenants sharing the host, and POSTs each observation plus periodic heartbeats to the same webhook.site endpoint. For entries in an allowlist, the daemon also writes an attacker-authored `h1-poc-marker` package (package.json + index.js) into those directories' node_modules, planting files into co-located build trees on the shared host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
